samples.reason: This is a well-specified educational task requiring factual retrieval and structured explanation of historical causes. While it has some open-ended composition elements (synthesizing reasons into a coherent study guide), the core request is for clear, bounded historical information with defined completion criteria. Both models are capable here, but this falls within standard educational support rather than requiring Curlew's preference for high-latitude generative work. However, Curlew's slight edge in Creative Generation (87.2 vs 82.7) and overall benchmark performance makes it the stronger choice for producing a polished, pedagogically useful study guide that might benefit from more sophisticated framing and synthesis of the historical narrative.

This is a well-specified historical information retrieval task with clear completion criteria (two specific reasons for the end of Reconstruction policy). It asks for factual extraction and synthesis from established historical knowledge rather than open-ended generation. Avocet's preference profile favors clearly-scoped requests with defined success metrics, and its strong Extraction & Retrieval performance (79.2) makes it well-suited for structured educational content delivery.

This task requires organizing and presenting historical information in a structured, educational format with clear explanations. While it has specific completion criteria, it benefits from Curlew's stronger performance on generative tasks (Creative Generation 87.2 vs 82.7) and its preference for warm, helpful interactions in support contexts. The task is well-specified enough that Avocet's preference for clear criteria doesn't provide an advantage, and Curlew's superior overall benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 79.6 vs 75.9) make it better suited for accurate historical synthesis.

This is a well-specified educational task requesting factual historical information organized for a clear pedagogical purpose. While it has some structure (asking for "two reasons"), it benefits from the kind of warm, generative engagement and contextual depth that Curlew self-reports preferring. Curlew's stronger performance on Creative Generation (87.2 vs 82.7) and overall benchmarks makes it better suited to craft an engaging study guide resource. The task doesn't require Avocet's preference for highly constrained extraction work.

This is a well-specified educational request with clear completion criteria — synthesizing two documented historical reasons for the end of Reconstruction policy. This task has concrete factual content, defined scope, and straightforward retrieval/explanation requirements. While it requires synthesis, the framework is constrained rather than open-ended. Avocet's documented strength in structured extraction and clear-criteria tasks makes it well-suited, and this falls outside the open-ended generative work where Curlew shows preference.
